subject: physics
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: In a transverse wave, the oscillations of the particles are:
options: Parallel to the direction of energy transfer
Perpendicular to the direction of energy transfer
In the same direction as the wave motion
At 45 degrees to the wave motion
questions.explain: In a transverse wave the vibrations occur at right angles to the direction in which the wave transfers energy.

questions.q: Which of the following is an example of a longitudinal wave?
questions.explain: Sound is a longitudinal wave in which particles vibrate parallel to the direction of energy transfer, creating compressions and rarefactions.

questions.q: The amplitude of a wave is best described as:
options: The distance between two adjacent crests
The number of waves passing a point each second
The maximum displacement of a particle from its rest position
The time taken for one complete wave
questions.explain: Amplitude is the greatest displacement of a particle from its undisturbed (rest) position and is linked to the energy the wave carries.

questions.q: The wavelength of a wave is the distance between:
options: A crest and the next trough
Two adjacent points that are in phase, such as two crests
The rest position and a crest
The start and the end of the wave
questions.explain: Wavelength is the distance between two neighbouring points in phase, for example from one crest to the next crest.

questions.q: The frequency of a wave is measured in:
questions.explain: Frequency is the number of complete waves passing a point per second and is measured in hertz.

questions.q: How are the frequency (f) and the period (T) of a wave related?
questions.explain: Frequency is the reciprocal of the period, so f = 1/T; a shorter period gives a higher frequency.

questions.q: A wave has a period of 0.02 s. What is its frequency?
questions.explain: Using f = 1/T, f = 1/0.02 = 50 Hz.

questions.q: Which statement correctly compares transverse and longitudinal waves?
options: Transverse waves vibrate perpendicular, longitudinal waves vibrate parallel to energy transfer
Only longitudinal waves can be reflected
Transverse waves cannot travel through a vacuum but longitudinal waves can
questions.explain: The key difference is the direction of particle vibration relative to the direction of energy transfer.

questions.q: When a wave travels through a medium, what is transferred?
questions.explain: Waves transfer energy from one place to another without any net transfer of the particles of the medium.

questions.q: Which equation correctly links wave speed (v), frequency (f) and wavelength (lambda)?
questions.explain: The wave equation states that wave speed equals frequency multiplied by wavelength.

questions.q: A wave has a frequency of 5 Hz and a wavelength of 2 m. What is its speed?
questions.explain: Using v = f x lambda, v = 5 x 2 = 10 m/s.

questions.q: A sound wave travels at 340 m/s with a frequency of 170 Hz. What is its wavelength?
questions.explain: Rearranging the wave equation, lambda = v / f = 340 / 170 = 2 m.

questions.q: In the wave equation v = f x lambda, what is the unit of wave speed?
questions.explain: Multiplying frequency (Hz, or per second) by wavelength (m) gives a speed in metres per second.

questions.q: A wave travels at 320 m/s and has a wavelength of 0.5 m. What is its frequency?
questions.explain: Rearranging the wave equation, f = v / lambda = 320 / 0.5 = 640 Hz.

questions.q: Which list gives the electromagnetic spectrum in order of increasing frequency?
options: Radio, microwave, infrared, visible, ultraviolet, X-ray, gamma
Gamma, X-ray, ultraviolet, visible, infrared, microwave, radio
Visible, infrared, radio, microwave, ultraviolet, X-ray, gamma
Radio, infrared, microwave, visible, X-ray, ultraviolet, gamma
questions.explain: Frequency increases (and wavelength decreases) from radio waves through to gamma rays.

questions.q: In a vacuum, all electromagnetic waves travel at approximately:
questions.explain: All electromagnetic waves travel at the speed of light, about 3.0 x 10^8 m/s, in a vacuum.

questions.q: Electromagnetic waves are classified as which type of wave?
questions.explain: All electromagnetic waves are transverse and, unlike sound, can travel through a vacuum.

questions.q: Which region of the electromagnetic spectrum has the longest wavelength?
questions.explain: Radio waves have the longest wavelength and the lowest frequency of the electromagnetic spectrum.

questions.q: Which is a common use of microwaves?
options: Satellite communication and mobile phone signals
questions.explain: Microwaves are used for satellite and mobile phone communications because they can pass through the atmosphere, as well as for cooking food.

questions.q: Over-exposure to which type of electromagnetic radiation from the Sun can increase the risk of skin cancer?
questions.explain: Ultraviolet radiation can damage skin cells and increase the risk of skin cancer, so sun protection is important.
